review.feedback: The two lemmas are mathematically correct. In the first, q | w*p and a≥1 give q | w*p^a, so i ≡ 2 (mod q) and i−1 ≡ 1 (mod q); hence q divides neither i nor i−1. Since q is prime, q cannot divide either reduced factor i/gcd(i,3) or (i−1)/gcd(i−1,6), so q ∤ Q. The second follows by contraposition: if q^3 | Q and q≠2, then q | w*p would contradict the first lemma, so q is coprime to w*p. The positivity assumptions w≥1 and a≥1, primality of q, q≠2, and the parametrization are all present and sufficient. The expressions match the Q from the imported context. The names are shorthand but the theorem types do not assert more than what is proved; in particular they do not claim the full v15 result.
